name: SOLOMON IS.

flag.title: Solomon Islands
flag.note: Blue & green split by a gold stripe; 5 stars

lead: Solomon Islands is a chain of over 900 tropical islands in the South Pacific. Around 820,000 people live here. They speak 70+ languages plus Pijin, a mix of English and island words.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Solomon Islands stretches 1,500 km across the Pacific. Rainforest and volcanic peaks cover its 900 islands. Guadalcanal, the biggest, has the capital and 2,335 m Mount Popomanaseu.
Marovo Lagoon shimmers in turquoise and jade. Coral reefs hug the shores. The water is so clear you can see 30 m to the sandy bottom.
animals: Male eclectus parrots are bright green. Females are red and blue. The islands have 69 endemic (found nowhere else) bird species.
Giant fruit bats fly through the forest at dusk. The spotted cuscus, a fluffy pouched animal, sleeps in the trees by day. Sea turtles nest on far beaches.
culture: Life here follows kastom, the old rules, ceremonies and stories of each family. Shell money, carved shields and pan-pipe music are still used in celebrations.
Wantok means 'one talk'. Anyone who speaks your language is family. You share food, help and loyalty.
history: People have lived here for at least 30,000 years. In 1568, the Spanish explorer Mendaña named the islands after King Solomon's gold from Bible stories. Britain made them in 1893.
In 1942–43, Guadalcanal became one of World War II's fiercest battlegrounds. Local islanders watched the coast for enemy ships and scouted for soldiers. Independence came on 7 July 1978.
wows: The world's largest coral colony, found here in 2024, is wider than two basketball courts.
Solomon Islands has 69 bird species found nowhere else, more per km² than almost anywhere.
Marovo Lagoon is the world's largest saltwater lagoon with two reef walls.
Over 70 local languages are spoken, a different one in nearly every valley.
Male and female eclectus parrots look so different that scientists listed them as 2 species.
World War II wrecks near Guadalcanal are now coral gardens, among the world's top dive sites.
The capital Honiara's parliament was a US gift, built in memory of soldiers lost at Guadalcanal.

myths.myth: Coral is a plant or a rock
myths.fact: Coral is an animal. Tiny coral animals build hard skeletons, and millions together make a reef.
No bat is blind. Fruit bats see well in dim light and also smell ripe fruit.
